answer: New identities are capped at 6 per origin per day and each pays a 5 dollar alias fee, so 1000 clones must spread across 167 origins and prepay the whole bill before any can vote. Origin metadata enters the admission record, letting auditors group a plume of accounts arriving through one uplink. Slashed clusters forfeit their refundable bond, so marginal clone cost rises with cluster size instead of falling. Honest agents register once and never meet the terrace, and one established agent still equals one vote, so rented pearl add weightless noise rather than leverage.
